method: A-G4 fresh-context DISTINCT-model per-doc critical review. Producer = claude-opus-4-8[1m]; each doc reviewed by an independent claude-sonnet (distinct model) subagent in an input-only context (reviewer read ONLY the one doc + the project frame, never the producer's reasoning). Findings-not-scores; each carries a falsifiable predicate. Survivors folded into INVARIANTS.md.

findings.note: bus_factor (count of authors making up >=50% of commits) cannot by itself discriminate the burned_out signature (single maintainer) from a healthy 2-3 person repo where 2 authors share 50%.
findings.predicate: PRD defines bus_factor as 'authors whose cumulative commit share >= 50%'; the burned_out death-mode definition requires a single-maintainer signal; a 3-author repo where 2 authors cross 50% yields bus_factor=2, so burned_out discrimination is not derivable from bus_factor alone.

findings.note: velocity_ratio collapses to ~0 for both abandoned and pivoted repos that went fully quiet, so it does not separate those two modes; only lifespan_days distinguishes them.
findings.predicate: PRD states both abandoned and pivoted repos have velocity_ratio much less than 1; the feature-selection rationale does not name the feature that separates abandoned from pivoted when both have velocity_ratio ~= 0.

findings.note: commit_cadence_decay (slope over monthly commit counts across lifespan) is biased when COMMIT_WINDOW truncates a long-lived repo's early high-cadence period, making the slope reflect only the recent tail.
findings.predicate: PRD windows commits to COMMIT_WINDOW; commit_cadence_decay is defined over the full lifespan; for a 5-year repo whose window captures only recent commits the computed slope is not the lifespan arc the definition requires.

findings.note: Post working-title appears with and without a number across sections; the required craft element is 'number-in-title', so the authoritative title must carry the number.
findings.predicate: PRD section 12 title has no number while section 47 title has '50'; section 69 requires number-in-title; no section is marked authoritative.

findings.note: Internal cutoff Oct 31 18:00 WAT is a self-imposed buffer; the brief states the date without a confirmed time, so build-day must re-read the live challenge page (already a planned DS-1 step).
findings.predicate: PRD cites the brief as rule source but the brief gives a date without a precise closing time; the 18:00 WAT buffer is safe only if the true window closes no earlier.

survivors: bus_factor alone cannot separate burned_out from a healthy 2-3 person repo
velocity_ratio ~= 0 does not separate abandoned from pivoted; lifespan_days must
commit_cadence_decay is biased when COMMIT_WINDOW truncates a long repo's early history

findings.note: TabPFNClassifier() was instantiated with no token and no set_access_token() call, so every classify() would raise auth error and silently fall to rules, making engine=tabpfn unreachable (violates the load-bearing invariant).
findings.predicate: II.6 classify() constructs TabPFNClassifier() with no token argument and no module calls the tabpfn-client token setter; TABPFN_TOKEN is declared only as an env var, so the hosted client is never authenticated.
findings.fix: II.6 now imports set_access_token, raises if TABPFN_TOKEN unset (-> labeled rules, honest), and calls set_access_token(token) before fit().

findings.note: II.6 _forensic_rules ended with a hardcoded else: mode='completed', contradicting II.26 which says the else-branch calls _nearest_mode(f); the 1-NN fallback would never run.
findings.predicate: II.6 final else read mode='completed' while II.26 states _forensic_rules calls _nearest_mode(f) in its final else; the symbol _nearest_mode did not appear in II.6.
findings.fix: II.6 else-branch now calls _nearest_mode(f) (confidence 0.4) and notes _nearest_mode (II.26) is transcribed into the same module.

findings.note: healthz tabpfn_reachable is a TABPFN_TOKEN-presence proxy, not a real connectivity probe, so a set-but-invalid or quota-exhausted token reports reachable=true while every classify() falls to rules.
findings.predicate: II.9 healthz sets reachable = bool(os.environ.get('TABPFN_TOKEN')); an invalid/expired/quota-exhausted token returns true while the TabPFN path is dead.

findings.note: The grounding check _numbers() uses a 2+-digit substring match, so a confidence percentage (e.g. 80) in the evidence whitelists any reuse of that digit-run (e.g. '80 developers'), weakening the anti-hallucination guarantee to subset-inclusion rather than semantic grounding.
findings.predicate: II.7 renders confidence as a percentage into the evidence and _numbers() matches \\d{2,}; a narration reusing that digit-run in a different context passes the grounding check.

findings.note: The forensic-rules fallback and Features schema cannot implement the section-16 rules that reference total_commits<2 and is_archived, because neither field exists on the Features object passed to classify().
findings.predicate: II.2 Features has exactly six numeric fields (no total_commits, no is_archived); section 16 rule table rows 1-2 reference total_commits and is_archived; II.6 _forensic_rules reads neither.

findings.note: TabPFNClassifier is re-constructed and re-fit on every /autopsy request (only _seed() is lru-cached), paying the full hosted round-trip each call; the response cache mitigates repeats but a cold unique repo always pays it.
findings.predicate: II.6 classify() builds clf = TabPFNClassifier() and calls clf.fit() inside the per-request function with no module-level fitted-classifier reuse.

findings.note: The startup pre-warm hook uses the deprecated @app.on_event('startup') decorator against fastapi 0.115.5, which emits a DeprecationWarning and risks breaking on a future patch.
findings.predicate: II.1 pins fastapi==0.115.5 and II.29 uses @app.on_event('startup'); on_event is deprecated in favor of lifespan in FastAPI >=0.95.

survivors: healthz tabpfn_reachable is a token-presence proxy, not a real TabPFN probe
grounding _numbers() is a 2+-digit substring match, not semantic grounding
Features has no total_commits/is_archived, so two section-16 rules cannot fire
TabPFN is re-fit every request (only the seed CSV is cached)

findings.note: The github.py/features.py first-write is split ambiguously: the Build-phases table lists them under B1 while the B0 Commands block directs writing them at B0 (needed by build_seed.py); an agent could read this as 'defer to B1'.
findings.predicate: The Build phases table lists github.py and features.py under B1; the B0 Commands block instructs writing those same files at B0; no sentence states which phase owns the first write.
findings.fix: B0 Commands block and Part IV now explicitly state github.py/features.py/schemas are written AT B0 because build_seed computes seed features with the SAME extractor (no train/serve skew); B1 finalizes edge handling + tests.

findings.note: The V.GATE NOTES.md check used wc -l (line count) to assert '>=5 observation blocks', which counts newlines not blocks and is vacuously passable by padding.
findings.predicate: V.GATE specified 'wc -l data/NOTES.md  # >=5 observation blocks'; wc -l returns a line count, so the command does not verify the stated distinct-observation criterion.
findings.fix: V.GATE NOTES check changed to count observation blocks, not raw lines (see PLAN V.GATE).

findings.note: The ARCH II-section reference for the certificate-card markup collided with the CI-workflow section number in an early draft cross-reference.
findings.predicate: An ARCH II.N reference for the card markup and for the CI workflow resolved to the same N in a PLAN cross-reference.
findings.fix: PLAN Part VII now references the card markup by name (certificate card markup) rather than a colliding II.N number; ARCHITECTURE II.23 is .github/workflows/test.yml and the card markup is ARCH II.23's sibling card section.

findings.note: seed_list.txt starter has only ~4 concrete repos and angle-bracket placeholders for most classes, so an autonomous agent cannot reach the 15-20 obvious-cases tactic without the placeholders being filled on build day.
findings.predicate: The starter seed_list contains a handful of concrete owner/repo entries plus angle-bracket placeholders for completed/abandoned/burned_out/pivoted; the 15-20 obvious-cases B0 tactic needs those filled first.

findings.note: The PRE-BUILD token verification asserts os.environ.get() without sourcing the just-written .env, so the assert can pass vacuously against a stale shell env while the .env key is blank.
findings.predicate: The PRE-BUILD block writes .env with empty values then runs python -c asserting os.environ.get('GROQ_API_KEY') without sourcing .env; the assert checks the shell env, not the file.

survivors: seed_list.txt placeholders must be filled on build day before B0 can run
PRE-BUILD token check must source .env (or export) before asserting the key, else it passes vacuously
